concerns.text: Phase 6 (Hypergraph Simulation) violates the 'Producer before Consumer' and 'Foundational tasks first' principles. It introduces a new artifact flow (T042-T047) that is not grounded in the spec.md or plan.md requirements. The tasks depend on T015 (filtered data) but the entire phase is an untraceable scope creep that breaks the independent-shippable unit of the User Stories defined in spec.md. This phase must be removed or explicitly linked to a new User Story/FR.

T004d (Implement data schema validators) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T004a and T004b (Generate schemas). A task cannot be parallel-safe if it consumes artifacts generated by other tasks in the same phase. The [P] tag is incorrect and creates a hidden ordering violation.

T016 (Checksum verification) is listed after T012 (Downloader) but before T013 (Parser). While the text notes the dependency, the visual ordering in the list (T012 -> T016 -> T013) is correct, but T016 is marked [P] in the list header line 'T016 [P] [US1]...' (implied by the [P] column logic in the header, though the text says 'removed [P] tag' in notes). If T016 is marked [P], it violates the dependency on T012. The task description says 'removed [P] tag' but the list format needs to ensure T016 is NOT marked [P] to respect the T012->T016 flow.

T026 (Sensitivity analysis) depends on T025 (fit_summary.csv). T025 is marked [ ] (not started) and T026 is marked [ ]. However, T026 is marked [P] in the list (implied by the column structure if not explicitly removed). Sensitivity analysis consumes the output of the fitting engine; it cannot be parallel-safe with the fitting engine or the metric calculator. The [P] tag must be removed to respect the T025->T026 dependency.

The comment '⚠️ CRITICAL SEQUENCE: T012 -> T016 -> T013 -> T014 -> T015' is helpful, but the task list itself should visually reflect this strict ordering (e.g., by removing [P] tags from all tasks in this sequence). Currently, T012 and T016 are listed with [P] in the header row logic, which contradicts the sequential requirement.
